finding: Round 15's `unsupported-mechanism-claim` (medium) named TWO sentences as disproven by measurement; the recorded fix corrected one and left the other verbatim. §7.1:193-195 still reads "registered `workflow.checks` run in the review phase only, while the list is written afterwards, so review would only ever see the check reporting `PENDING`". Re-measured this round in a clone of HEAD with the guard list UNWRITTEN -- exactly today's state and exactly the state the sentence describes: guard-document window moved to v0.31.2 -> exit 1, no PENDING line; §7.1's own window reworded past `between the `<from>` and `<to>` tags` -> exit 1, no PENDING; `--no-ext-diff` dropped from the documented command -> exit 1, no PENDING; the match rule reworded -> exit 1, no PENDING; the count made stale -> exit 1. PENDING is the baseline state, not the only state, so the surviving sentence is still false. It now also contradicts the paragraph three lines below it, which the same repair rewrote to say the opposite -- "It did guard the window, rule and count claims in that time" -- since guarding is precisely review seeing the check in a state other than PENDING. The surviving half is the load-bearing one: it is the stated premise for "The observer for that rule ... has to be" the first task's acceptance, and §8.1 now generalises it into a standing rule.

resolved.evidence: Section 7.1's remaining sentence is corrected to match the paragraph below it: no review round can see the list compared against the derivation. It no longer claims review would only ever see PENDING, which measurement disproved.

suggestion: Narrow the sentence to what measurement supports: review can never see the LIST checked, because the list is written after review closes -- not that the check only ever reports PENDING. e.g. "... while the list is written afterwards, so review can never see the list itself checked, only the claims around it." Keep it consistent with the corrected paragraph below.

finding: The paragraph the round-15 repair added to §8.1 carries the exact claim the same repair retracted from §7.1. §8.1:258-261 justifies the CLAUDE.md qualifier "since a check registered where the thing it measures does not yet exist suppresses a finding class for every reviewer and verifies nothing." §7.1 no longer says that: "the registration could never verify the list -- the artifact does not exist during review ... It did guard the window, rule and count claims in that time, so the trade was real rather than free." Re-measured this round with the list unwritten, the registered check fails on four distinct edits a review round actually makes (window moved, window reworded past its pattern, `--no-ext-diff` dropped, match rule reworded), so "verifies nothing" is false for the single instance the rule generalises from -- and rounds 8 and 10 closed high findings on exactly that guard. This bites harder here than in §7.1: §8.1 is now the canonical home of the rule and it mandates the CLAUDE.md edit, so the reason written here is the reason the next cycle acts on. As written the phase condition is absolute ("verifies nothing"), where §7.1's corrected account makes it a trade -- real value, outweighed by suppression. The two homes of the one fact disagree in the release whose §8.1 exists to stop exactly that.

resolved.evidence: Section 8.1's justification no longer says the check verifies nothing. It says a check registered before its subject exists verifies only whatever part already exists -- which may be nothing, and was not enough here.

suggestion: State the operative ground and match §7.1: a check registered in a phase where the artifact it certifies does not yet exist suppresses a finding class for every reviewer while being unable to verify that artifact, so the registration is weighed against what it does guard rather than assumed to guard nothing. Drop "and verifies nothing".
